# sq-48 — Corpus harness flags entries with no golden

The private-corpus harness (sq-18) reports an entry that has no golden as "no golden" (not passed), and a run with any such entry says so in its summary; an option can make that a failure. **Not in this slice:** recording goldens for the private corpus.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-10-30** — Gate round 1: FAIL on R1 (a new test set SQUALIFY_UPDATE_GOLDEN and SQUALIFY_CORPUS process-wide while other tests run in parallel, so a golden test could rewrite a tracked golden and pass; fix: pure overloads, no env in tests). Fix round also takes R3 (UPDATE_GOLDEN rewrites every golden, wording), R4 (summary wording when only the env var is set), G7 (split the theory so the raw test name says no-golden). Later, not in this slice: R5 corpus-check.sh and the theory's recording path have no automated test; R6 a golden added or removed between listing and running mislabels the relabel (counts stay right); R7 an empty corpus writes no summary.

## Why

Today an entry with no golden passes, so a green corpus run only shows that profiling did not crash. A consumer review (2026-10-30) read a green run as coverage of a format family that had no goldens at all.

- Entries with a golden behave as today (pass or fail on the comparison); the determinism checks are unchanged.
- The harness never writes data-derived output outside the corpus directory (as today).
- Mutation-check each test (an entry with no golden counted as passed makes a test red).
